duplicate_route_name.impact: Riders can see indistinguishable routes, and consumers may merge or label distinct services ambiguously.
duplicate_route_name.fix: Give routes in the same agency and mode a unique short/long-name combination. Model opposite directions as trips of one route, not as duplicate routes.

empty_row.impact: Whitespace-only records are interpreted differently by CSV readers and can become malformed phantom rows.
empty_row.fix: Remove the blank or whitespace-only physical line from the source file before creating the GTFS archive.

fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.impact: Journey planners may show impossible travel times; the issue often reveals swapped coordinates or an incorrect timestamp.
fast_travel_between_consecutive_stops.fix: Verify both stop coordinates and the consecutive arrival/departure times. Correct the value that creates the unrealistic speed.

fast_travel_between_far_stops.impact: A long-distance segment with an impossible speed can corrupt routing, ETAs, and map display for the whole trip.
fast_travel_between_far_stops.fix: Check for a wrong stop_id, misplaced stop coordinates, or a missing hour in the second stop time.

leading_or_trailing_whitespaces.impact: Identifiers that differ only by spaces can break foreign-key matching, while rider-facing text may display unevenly.
leading_or_trailing_whitespaces.fix: Trim whitespace at both ends of the value in the source system; do not rely on the validator to normalize the published feed.

missing_bike_allowance.impact: Riders cannot tell whether a bicycle is accepted on ferry journeys.
missing_bike_allowance.fix: Set trips.bikes_allowed to 1 or 2 for ferry trips according to the operator policy.

missing_feed_contact_email_and_url.impact: Feed consumers have no reliable operational contact when they find a data problem.
missing_feed_contact_email_and_url.fix: Add feed_contact_email, feed_contact_url, or both to feed_info.txt and keep the contact monitored.

missing_recommended_column.impact: The feed remains parseable, but consumers lose information recommended for a complete rider experience.
missing_recommended_column.fix: Use the filename and fieldName values in the report to add the named column, then populate it wherever the data is available.
missing_recommended_column.file: the file named in the notice

missing_recommended_file.impact: The core schedule can still work, but consumers may miss recommended metadata or service detail.
missing_recommended_file.fix: Use the filename value in the notice to add the recommended file. If the feature truly does not apply, document that decision.
missing_recommended_file.file: the file named in the notice

mixed_case_recommended_field.impact: ALL-CAPS or all-lowercase customer text is harder to scan and performs poorly in screen readers and voice interfaces.
mixed_case_recommended_field.fix: Rewrite rider-facing names in natural mixed case while preserving official capitalization and acronyms.
mixed_case_recommended_field.file: the file named in the notice

non_ascii_or_non_printable_char.impact: Hidden control characters in identifiers can make two values look identical while breaking joins between GTFS files.
non_ascii_or_non_printable_char.fix: Remove control characters from ID fields. Replace decorative Unicode in identifiers with stable printable ASCII values.
non_ascii_or_non_printable_char.file: the file named in the notice

platform_without_parent_station.impact: Consumers cannot group the platform into a station, which weakens station navigation and transfer presentation.
platform_without_parent_station.fix: Create or identify the parent station row and set the platform's parent_station to that station's stop_id.

route_color_contrast.impact: Route labels may be unreadable in maps and lists, especially for riders with low vision.
route_color_contrast.fix: Choose route_color and route_text_color with sufficient contrast; test the exact hexadecimal pair used in routes.txt.

route_long_name_contains_short_name.impact: Apps commonly combine both fields, producing labels such as “10 — Route 10 Downtown”.
route_long_name_contains_short_name.fix: Keep the identifier in route_short_name and describe only the destination or corridor in route_long_name.

route_short_name_too_long.impact: Long route labels are truncated or wrap badly in compact signs, maps, and mobile interfaces.
route_short_name_too_long.fix: Put the concise public route designator in route_short_name and move the descriptive text to route_long_name.

stop_too_far_from_shape.impact: Vehicles can appear off-route and walking directions may lead riders away from the actual boarding point.
stop_too_far_from_shape.fix: Verify the stop coordinates and the trip's shape_id. Move the wrong point or redraw the shape so it follows the served stops.

stop_too_far_from_shape_using_user_dista.impact: The stop falls outside the custom shape-distance tolerance selected for this validation run.
stop_too_far_from_shape_using_user_dista.fix: Check stop coordinates and the referenced shape first. Increase the custom tolerance only when the wider distance is intentional.

Configured tolerance: 25 m
Measured stop-to-shape distance: 62 m
stop_too_far_from_shape_using_user_dista.good:

stop_without_stop_time.impact: The stop is never served and can clutter maps or indicate a misspelled stop_id in stop_times.txt.
stop_without_stop_time.fix: Reference the stop from the intended trip, or remove the stops.txt row if the location is no longer published.
stop_without_stop_time.bad:
stops.txt: S_UNUSED,Old Terminal,35.17,33.36
stop_times.txt: no row references S_UNUSED

unknown_column.impact: Consumers ignore unrecognized columns, so data placed there may never reach riders.
unknown_column.fix: Correct a misspelled GTFS field name. If it is a deliberate extension, use an extension documented for your target consumers.
unknown_column.file: the file named in the notice

unused_stop.impact: The feed carries a location that is not served and is not needed as a parent, increasing noise and the chance of stale data.
unused_stop.fix: Remove the stop if obsolete, or reference it from the correct stop_times row. This notice is produced in thorough mode.
unused_stop.bad:
stops.txt: S2,Unused Stop,35.18,33.37
stop_times.txt: no row references S2
